::: {.hero}
<p class="name">Joris Klingen</p>
<p class="role">Economist at CPB Netherlands Bureau for Economic Policy Analysis</p>

::: {.chips}
<span>Transport economics</span><span>Urban economics</span><span>Environmental economics</span><span>Road safety</span><span>Cycling</span>
:::
:::

I am an economist at the **CPB Netherlands Bureau for Economic Policy Analysis**.
I have a PhD from [Spatial Economics, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam](https://spatialeconomics.nl/), where I was supervised by Jos van Ommeren and Erik Verhoef.
Before my PhD, I studied Economics and Econometrics at the [Tinbergen Institute](https://www.tinbergen.nl), Spatial Transport and Environmental Economics at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, and Future Planet Studies at the Universiteit van Amsterdam.
In 2019, I visited Imperial College London, where I worked with Dan Graham at the [Transport Strategy Centre](https://www.imperial.ac.uk/transport-engineering/transport-strategy-centre/).

My research is empirical work in transport and environmental economics.
So far I have studied road safety, the immediate effects of air pollution, and urban cycling.
For the latter, I use public data from bicycle-sharing schemes in major cities (Paris, London, New York City).
See [Research](research.qmd) for papers and work in progress.

For fun, I am also a musician (see [Music](music.qmd)).
